settings_sub: Changes apply right away, no restart needed unless marked
changed_elsewhere: The same settings were changed in another window.
restart_needed: Restart the app to use the new dashboard port
leave_body: Your edits in Settings will be lost.
f_interval_hint: Seconds between checks (1–3600). Lower is faster to detect, heavier on the network.
f_fail_hint: Consecutive failed checks needed to report an outage.
f_loss_hint: Above this the connection is reported unstable.
f_latency_hint: Above this the connection is reported unstable.
f_icmp_hint: Tells router problems apart from provider problems. May need admin rights.
f_webhook_hint: Posts every outage to a Discord or Slack channel. Any other address gets a plain JSON message (title, text and the raw data), which works with Home Assistant, n8n, Zapier, IFTTT and similar. Use https, or http for an address on your own network.
f_tg_hint: Sends the same alerts through your Telegram bot.
secret_will_remove: Will be removed when you save
sound_upload_hint: MP3 or WAV, up to 30 seconds and 10 MB
sound_uploaded: Custom sound saved — alerts will use it
f_speed_duration_hint: 5–120 seconds. Longer is more accurate on fast lines.
f_speed_upload_hint: Leave empty to skip the upload test.
f_logdir_hint: A folder inside the app folder.
f_auto_update_hint: Asks GitHub for a new version every 6 hours. Turn off to stop it; the button below still works.
update_in_progress: An update is already in progress.
update_failed_plain: The update didn't finish. Try again later.
config_error: Your config.json is damaged, so defaults are in use: {error}
sound_err_format: This file isn't a playable MP3 or WAV, or it's longer than 30 seconds.
sound_err_size: The file is empty or larger than 10 MB.
sound_preview_failed: This window couldn't play the sound — try “Play like a real alert”.
sound_play_failed: The app couldn't play the sound. Check that your computer isn't muted.
sound_check_failed: Couldn't check which sound is active
sound_reset_body: Alerts will play the default sound again.
startup_on: Internet Monitor will start with Windows
startup_off: Internet Monitor won't start with Windows
f_speed_data: Each test uses about {per} of data at {speed} Mbps.
f_speed_data_month: Each test uses about {per} of data at {speed} Mbps, so the schedule uses about {month} a month. On a capped plan this counts toward your quota.
f_ntfy_hint: Install the free ntfy app on your phone, subscribe to a topic with a name that's hard to guess, and paste its address here. Works with ntfy.sh or your own ntfy server.
f_ntfy_token_hint: Only needed if your ntfy topic is protected.
f_seal_ts_hint: Every day's logs are sealed with a hash chain. With this on, each day's seal is also timestamped by an independent authority (freetsa.org), which receives only a 32-byte hash, never your data. That timestamp lets anyone check that your logs existed in this exact form on that date.
update_store: This copy comes from the Microsoft Store, which installs updates for you.
f_startup_store: Turn it on or off in Windows Settings → Apps → Startup.
ra_title: Coming soon: alerts even when the power is out
ra_body: Today an alert can only leave your home once the internet is back, so you hear about a long outage after it ends. An optional outside service could notice when your home goes silent and alert your phone right away.
ra_hint: Opens a page on GitHub in your browser. The app itself sends nothing.
ra_thanks: Thanks — we'll mention it in What's new
phone_sub: Scan this code with your phone's camera while it's on the same Wi-Fi. To keep the dashboard one tap away, choose “Add to Home screen” in your phone's browser.
phone_qr_alt: QR code that opens the dashboard on your phone
phone_warning_title: This code contains your access key
phone_warning: Anyone on your network who scans it can open your dashboard, so don't share a photo of it. If your phone later says to open the dashboard from the app, the key has changed: scan the code again.
